CFML Language Reference: Tags

CFCOL

Each CFCOL inside a CFTABLE describes one column: its heading, its width and alignment, and the text to show for every row. The TEXT is evaluated once per row, so it can mix column names, functions and literal text.

Category

Output and page processing

Syntax

<CFCOL HEADER="column_header"
    WIDTH="number_of_characters"
    ALIGN="Left/Right/Center"
    TEXT="#column_text#">

Attributes

HEADER
Optional. Heading for the column, shown when the CFTABLE has COLHEADERS.
WIDTH
Optional, default "20". Column width in characters. Text tables pad or cut the text to this width; HTML tables use it as a hint for the heading cell.
ALIGN
Optional, default "Left". Left, Right or Center.
TEXT
Optional. What to show in each row, usually built from query columns: TEXT="#LastName#, #FirstName#".

Usage

CFCOL is only valid inside CFTABLE; on its own it raises a context validation error. Columns appear in the order of the CFCOL tags. Right alignment makes number and money columns much easier to read.

Example

Opens the example in a new window. The example runs on this server, so it only works when you browse from the server itself (127.0.0.1).
<CFQUERY NAME="Courses" DATASOURCE="cfsnippets" MAXROWS="6">
SELECT CorNumber, CorName, CorLevel FROM CourseList ORDER BY CorNumber
</CFQUERY>
<P>Three alignments in a text table:</P>
<CFTABLE QUERY="Courses" COLHEADERS HEADERLINES="1">
  <CFCOL HEADER="No." WIDTH="6" ALIGN="Right" TEXT="#CorNumber#">
  <CFCOL HEADER="Course" WIDTH="34" ALIGN="Left" TEXT="#CorName#">
  <CFCOL HEADER="Level" WIDTH="14" ALIGN="Center" TEXT="#CorLevel#">
</CFTABLE>
